steps.title: Calculate the 90-day window
steps.change: The date window depends on the most recent transaction. The CTE returns one pair of dates for the whole report. Subtract 89 days because the latest date counts as one of the 90. Orders supplies the OrderDate values for this date-bound CTE; its one row is the latest date and the inclusive window bounds, not the outer customer population.

steps.title: Match only orders inside the window
steps.change: Every customer is a candidate for outreach, including Cia, who has never ordered. Only the customer list contains everyone to test.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT Customers.CustomerID, Orders.OrderID AS matched_order_id, Orders.OrderDate AS matched_order_date
FROM Customers
LEFT JOIN Orders
    ON Orders.CustomerID = Customers.CustomerID
   AND date(Orders.OrderDate) BETWEEN
       (SELECT window_start FROM reporting_window)
       AND (SELECT latest_order_date FROM reporting_window)
ORDER BY Customers.CustomerID;
steps.sql:
WITH reporting_window AS (
    SELECT date(MAX(OrderDate)) AS latest_order_date,
           date(MAX(OrderDate), '-89 days') AS window_start
    FROM Orders
)
SELECT Customers.CustomerID, Orders.OrderID AS matched_order_id, Orders.OrderDate AS matched_order_date
FROM Customers
LEFT JOIN Orders
    ON Orders.CustomerID = Customers.CustomerID
   AND date(Orders.OrderDate) BETWEEN
       (SELECT window_start FROM reporting_window)
       AND (SELECT latest_order_date FROM reporting_window)
ORDER BY Customers.CustomerID;

steps.title: Keep customers with no recent match
steps.change: Ben and Cia have no matching order inside the window, so their joined order IDs are NULL.
steps.sql:
WITH reporting_window AS (
    SELECT date(MAX(OrderDate)) AS latest_order_date,
           date(MAX(OrderDate), '-89 days') AS window_start
    FROM Orders
)
SELECT Customers.CustomerID, Orders.OrderID AS matched_order_id, Orders.OrderDate AS matched_order_date
FROM Customers
LEFT JOIN Orders
    ON Orders.CustomerID = Customers.CustomerID
   AND date(Orders.OrderDate) BETWEEN
       (SELECT window_start FROM reporting_window)
       AND (SELECT latest_order_date FROM reporting_window)
WHERE Orders.OrderID IS NULL
ORDER BY Customers.CustomerID;

steps.title: Select the customer details and sort
steps.change: A NULL order ID indicates the recent-order join found no match. Testing whether an order is outside the window could let a customer with both an old and a recent order through. The customer ID breaks sign-up date ties.
